Static/code-path review of the full `git diff origin/integration/nightshift` plus the untracked scripts/nightshift-project-context.py and docs/PROJECT-CONTEXT.md against docs/18/SPEC.md's acceptance criteria found no actionable blocking defects. Root identity precedence (explicit > neutral > legacy, conflict blocks unless explicit), scope containment, malformed/unreadable-manifest handling (no legacy fallback), the --shell mode's shlex.quote-based safe eval (verified no injection vector for `$()`/backticks/quotes), the semantic document-read lookup's exit-code contract (0/1/64) and identifier regex validation, the install.sh Bash-3.2 empty-array fix (`${UPDATE_ARGS[@]+"${UPDATE_ARGS[@]}"}` under `set -euo pipefail`), and dual-location installation of the resolver (shared $NIGHTSHIFT_TARGET/scripts and legacy $CLAUDE_SCRIPT_DST) and policy doc were all traced directly against source and match spec. Caller error propagation via `X=\"$(...)\" || exit $?` is consistently applied across every migrated script. The Confluence fetch in nightshift-product.md now goes through the generic `nightshift-capability.sh --resolve document-read` path instead of a hardcoded `mcp__claude_ai_Atlassian__getConfluencePage` call, satisfying the 'no provider-specific document tool in core' AC. Auth, retry-exhaust, preflight ordering, deploy-JSON precedence, worktree isolation, and legacy state-dir fallback logic are untouched except for the PROJECT-resolution line, preserving existing behavior. tests/test-project-context.sh (191 lines, read-only) provides direct behavioral coverage for every claim above including a live shell-injection attempt and a mode-000 unreadable-manifest case; I read it in full and traced each assertion against the resolver/capability implementation by hand, but I could NOT execute it or any other test in this sandbox — every `bash tests/test-project-context.sh` invocation and every Write of a temp fixture was rejected with 'requires approval' with no interactive channel to grant it, and /private/tmp/nightshift-18-green-evals.log (the separately-running full harness) was also unreadable (permission denied) from this session, so I have no retained execution evidence and am not claiming the suite passes — only that static tracing found no contract violation. Two minor, non-blocking observations for the engineer's awareness, neither rising to CONFLICT: (1) scripts/nightshift-crash-check.sh's header comment 'Fail-open: any error / non-pipeline project prints CLEAN' is no longer strictly true for a *standalone* invocation with conflicting NIGHTSHIFT_PROJECT_DIR/CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR (it now exits 1 via the resolver's PROJECT_CONFLICT instead of printing CLEAN), but every actual caller (nightshift-eng.md) already normalizes to the neutral var and clears the legacy one via `--shell` before invoking it, so the conflict path is unreachable in the shipped pipeline. (2) scripts/nightshift-capability.sh's `--resolve` branch relies on argparse for CLI parsing; a malformed invocation missing the required `operation` positional exits 2 via argparse's own SystemExit rather than the documented 64, but no shipped caller invokes it that way (all pass `document-read` explicitly) and it isn't exercised by the test file. Neither is a real user-facing regression against the spec's acceptance criteria.

claims.claim: resolve_project(): explicit --project always wins; with neither explicit, if NIGHTSHIFT_PROJECT_DIR and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR are both set and resolve to different physical directories, discovery raises PROJECT_CONFLICT and blocks; with neither set, falls back to `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, then cwd; --cwd-default skips the git-root fallback and preserves hook pwd-only behavior.

discover() rejects a --scope outside the resolved project (including via a symlink that resolves outside) with SCOPE_OUTSIDE_PROJECT, and returns AGENTS.md then CLAUDE.md per ancestor from project root to scope only (siblings excluded); unreadable/escaping convention files raise CONVENTION_INVALID.

TOML manifest handling: `.nightshift.toml` takes precedence over `nightshift.toml`; malformed/unreadable canonical manifest raises MANIFEST_INVALID with no fallback to the legacy file; `[tests]` must be a table and `command` must be a nonblank string without NUL/CR/LF, else TEST_COMMAND_INVALID; absent manifest yields manifest/test_command/test_command_source all null with status ok.

--shell mode emits `export NIGHTSHIFT_PROJECT_DIR=<shlex.quote(path)>` and `unset CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` only on success; directory() rejects paths containing NUL/CR/LF before they can reach the quoted output, and shlex.quote neutralizes `$()`, backticks, quotes and `;` for safe `eval`. No other branch prints to stdout in --shell/--root-only modes; blocked results print JSON to stderr only in those modes.

capability.sh's `--resolve document-read --mapping FILE --available-tools FILE` branch validates operation=='document-read', that mapping is a dict with only that key mapping to an identifier matching `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, and available-tools is a list of such identifiers; exits 0/status=available with the tool when present in both, exits 1/status=unavailable when missing inputs or tool absent from the inventory, exits 64/status=error with code CAPABILITY_CONFIG_INVALID for malformed JSON/unreadable files/invalid shapes/unknown operation. Performs no cache write, no CLI probe, no network call, no tool execution.

install.sh fixes a Bash-3.2 empty-array-under-`set -u` failure by changing `--configure "${UPDATE_ARGS[@]}"` to `--configure ${UPDATE_ARGS[@]+"${UPDATE_ARGS[@]}"}`, under an active `set -euo pipefail` at the top of the file.

nightshift-project-context.py is installed to both the shared runtime scripts dir (via the `nightshift-*.py` glob loop into $SCRIPT_DST=$NIGHTSHIFT_TARGET/scripts) and explicitly beside the legacy Claude script adapters ($CLAUDE_SCRIPT_DST); docs/PROJECT-CONTEXT.md is installed to `${NIGHTSHIFT_TARGET}/docs/nightshift-project-context.md`, matching the paths referenced from agents/*.md and commands/*.md via `${NIGHTSHIFT_HOME:-$HOME/.nightshift}/...`.

commands/nightshift-product.md's Confluence-URL branch no longer hardcodes `mcp__claude_ai_Atlassian__getConfluencePage`; it now resolves the operation through `scripts/nightshift-capability.sh --resolve document-read` with adapter-supplied mapping/available-tools files, validates the tool schema before use, and preserves the prior empty-context fallback on failure/unavailability.

Every migrated shell script (state-dir, triage, batch-init/resolve/retro/update, citations-trim, claim-cache, crash-check, lock-field, pw, retry-exhaust, scope-freeze/thaw, spec-digest, stop-hook, tdd-integrity-check/red-lock/spec-lock, tracker-trim) replaces the old `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$(git rev-parse ...||pwd)}` inline logic with `PROJECT="$(python3 .../nightshift-project-context.py --root-only ...)" || exit $?`, correctly propagating the resolver's exit code to the caller under both `set -e` and non-`-e` scripts.

scripts/nightshift-preflight-check.sh translates the legacy env var to the neutral one at the batch-resolve boundary using `env -u CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR NIGHTSHIFT_PROJECT_DIR="$PROJECT" bash .../nightshift-batch-resolve.sh`, replacing the old `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$PROJECT"` passthrough; HAVE_REF/HAVE_BATCH branching and downstream retry/auth logic are otherwise unmodified.
